facts.text: Rochdale Village was named after the English town of Rochdale, where the Rochdale Pioneers developed the principles of cooperation.
Rochdale Village was built on the former site of the Jamaica Race Course, which was once the area's only tourist site.
Designed as a city within a city, Rochdale Village was the largest private cooperative housing complex in the world until 1971.
Rochdale Village became a symbol of the Civil Rights Movement when protesters disrupted its construction in 1961.
Rochdale Village is known as the Jewel of Jamaica and consists of twenty buildings arranged in five circular groups.
A twenty-one megawatt cogeneration facility independently generates all the electricity, heating, and hot water for the entire Rochdale Village development.
